D.t: Phil Weiser leads by 21.4 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 608,347 votes; a one point swing is about 14,187 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +12.2 and D +30.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 231,372 votes; Boulder, a projected net 119,103 votes; Jefferson, a projected net 99,823 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +1.0, 11.8% of the vote; Douglas, D +2.3, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +0.9, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +10.2, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Phil Weiser runs furthest behind in Pueblo, Mesa, Weld. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.09 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Men, 49% of voters, 54 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.47 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Phil Weiser: Immigration voters 24 to 73, Small counties 46 to 50, Voters who can afford daily costs 49 to 48. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$725K cash against $158K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 32% of the 985,452 ballots in Colorado so far, against 24% for the other party. That is 4.5 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points toward Phil Weiser. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Money: Raised $1.1M against $1.7M for Phil Weiser.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Weld, a projected net 20,763 votes; Mesa, a projected net 14,198 votes; Fremont, a projected net 7,981 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +1.0, 11.8% of the vote; Douglas, D +2.3, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +0.9, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +10.2, 1.0% of the vote.

R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Victor Marx runs furthest behind in Arapahoe. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.
